{{Short description|Privately-run detention center in Washington, United States}}
{{Use American English|date=August 2025}}
[[File:GEO-Transport-bus-arriving-in-Portland-Oregon.jpg|thumb|A GEO Transport bus arrives from the Northwest Detention Center to pick up detained people from the ICE office at the 511 NW Broadway federal building in Portland, Oregon.]]

'''Northwest Detention Center''' is a privately-run detention center located in the Tideflats of the City of [[Tacoma, Washington]], USA.<ref>{{cite web |title=Map, Tideflats |url=https://cms.cityoftacoma.org/enviro/Tideflats.pdf |publisher=City of Tacoma, WA}}</ref> The detention center is operated by the [[GEO Group]] on behalf of the [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]].<ref>"[http://www.thegeogroupinc.com/facility.asp?fid=105 Northwest Detention Center]." [[GEO Group]]. Retrieved on November 22, 2010.</ref> The NWDC's current capacity is 1575, making it one of the largest detention centers in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nwirp.org/resources/about-the-nw-detention-center/|title=About the NW Detention Center {{!}} Northwest Immigrant Rights|website=www.nwirp.org|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref> Numerous hunger strikes have been launched by inmates of the NWDC to protest the Center's poor conditions. Detainees have repeatedly reported overcrowding, a lack of medical attention, and severely unsanitary conditions, especially during COVID-19: "they're not even offering us soap."<ref name="Raff">{{Cite web|title='Don't Let Us Die in Here': Coronavirus in ICE Detention - The Atlantic|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/video/index/610186/coronavirus-ice/|last=Raff|first=Jeremy|website=www.theatlantic.com|language=en|access-date=2020-05-06}}</ref>

== History ==
The detention center opened in 2004 by [[Correctional Services Corporation]] (CSC) under a contract with The [[United States Department of Homeland Security|US Department of Homeland Security]]. In 2005, CSC was purchased by the [[GEO Group]], thus acquiring the Northwest Detention Center.

In June 2008, the [[Seattle University School of Law]]'s International Human Rights Clinic published an investigation on the NWDC concluding that conditions they found, "violate both [[international human rights law]] and domestic Constitutional protections."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://law.seattleu.edu/documents/news/archive/2008/DRFinal.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100610075503/http://www.law.seattleu.edu/documents/news/archive/2008/DRFinal.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 10, 2010|title=Voices from Detention: A Report on Human Rights Violations at the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma, Washington|website=law.seattleu.edu|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref>

A contract with [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) expanded the detention center's housing capacity in 2009, making it the largest detention center owned by GEO Group on the West Coast.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.geogroup.com/maps/locationdetails/52|title=Northwest Detention Center - The GEO Group Inc.|website=www.geogroup.com|access-date=2016-08-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712161210/http://geogroup.com/Maps/LocationDetails/52|archive-date=2015-07-12|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In March 2014, inmates launched a hunger strike to protest conditions at NWDC. According to ICE, 750 detainees had refused meals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/03/10/immigrant-detainees-hunger-strike_n_4926968.html|title=Hundreds Of Immigrant Detainees Go On Hunger Strike|date=2014-03-08|website=The Huffington Post|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref> House Representative [[Adam Smith (Washington politician)|Adam Smith]] (D-9) criticized the NWDC in an interview with ''The Stranger'' in May, calling for improvement of the "shocking" conditions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://slog.thestranger.com/slog/archives/2014/03/25/rep-adam-smith-slams-shocking-conditions-at-immigrant-detention-center|title=Rep. Adam Smith Slams "Shocking" Conditions at Immigrant Detention Center|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref> Protesters are calling for better food, speedier trials, lower commissary prices, and increased wages for labor.

In April 2015, guards allegedly beat Alfredo Rodriguez, an undocumented Honduran immigrant in his 60s. Rodriguez had reportedly criticized a guard for mistreating an inmate who was mopping.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/northwest/tacoma-ice-center-faces-new-criticism-over-alleged-beating/|title=Tacoma immigrant detention center criticized over alleged violent incident|date=2015-05-19|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref> Rodriguez has since been deported, and Jennifer Lesmez, who represents six detainees who witnessed the incident, says some were threatened with retaliation if they complained.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thenewstribune.com/news/local/crime/article26292805.html|title=Tacoma immigrant detention center criticized over alleged violent incident|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref> U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement spokesman Andrew Muñoz disputed the account, adding that "ICE policies forbid retaliation" toward detainees.

In October 2015, the GEO Group renewed a ten-year contract with ICE.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20151001005937/en/GEO-Group-Signs-Contract-Continued-Management-Northwest|title=The GEO Group Signs Contract for the Continued Management of Northwest Detention Center {{!}} Business Wire|website=www.businesswire.com| date=October 2015 |access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref> The contract pays GEO for almost 1,200 beds daily, regardless if they are used.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2021-03-31|title=Northwest detention center in Tacoma slated to close under bill passed by Legislature|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/politics/legislature-passes-bill-that-will-close-northwest-detention-center-in-tacoma/|access-date=2021-05-08|website=The Seattle Times|language=en-US}}</ref>

On August 18, 2016, the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] announced that they would end privatization of federal prisons, however this would not affect immigrant detention centers, which were 62% privately operated in 2014 compared to 8% of federal prisoners.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thinkprogress.org/the-federal-government-is-not-actually-ending-private-prisons-40e8c8dbf976#.cmjxrwpn2|title=The Problem With The DOJ's Decision To Stop Using Private Prisons — ThinkProgress|last=Shen|first=Aviva|website=[[ThinkProgress]]|date=2016-08-18|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref> Geo stocks declined sharply after the announcement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.google.com/finance/quote/GEO:NYSE|title=The GEO Group Inc: NYSE:GEO quotes & news - Google Finance|website=www.google.com|access-date=2016-08-18}}</ref>

On September 20, 2017 WA State Attorney General Bob Ferguson filed a lawsuit against GEO Group, Inc., the [[private prison]] company that runs Tacoma's Northwest Detention Center (NWDC). The lawsuit alleges that GEO Group, Inc., the second-largest private prison provider in the country, has for years violated Washington State's minimum wage law, paying its workers $1 per day or in some instances, with snacks and extra food. "Let's be honest about what's going on," said Ferguson, speaking at a downtown Seattle news conference. "GEO has a captive population of vulnerable individuals who cannot easily advocate for themselves. This corporation is exploiting those workers for their own profits."<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/state-ag-bob-ferguson-files-lawsuit-against-company-that-operates-northwest-detention-center/ | title=State AG Bob Ferguson sues firm that operates Tacoma detention center for immigrants over $1 a day wages | date=20 September 2017 }}</ref>

On July 13, 2019 an armed individual allegedly [[2019 Tacoma attack|attempted to attack the detention center]] with a rifle and threw incendiary devices. The individual was killed during a confrontation with law enforcement. Four Tacoma police officers were placed on paid administrative leave.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2019/07/13/police-man-killed-attempted-tacoma-immigration-prison-attack/1724178001/|title=Police kill man who allegedly attempted to attack immigration prison with fire|website=USA TODAY|language=en|access-date=2019-07-13}}</ref>

On April 17, 2020, a group of female detainees began a hunger strike to protest the dangerous conditions they faced at the NWDC during the COVID-19 epidemic. The women reported severe overcrowding, a lack of access to medical care, and total disregard for sanitation.<ref name="Raff"/>
